name: flat-water-blockers
comment: BlockFlowing.blockBlocksFlow's id list (BlockFlowing.java:220-231: doorWood 64, doorSteel 71, signPost 63, ladder 65, reed 83 block flow whatever their material). A two-layer stone platform (y = 59, 60) with the rim at y = 61 and a water source at (0,61,0). In its path: a ladder at (0,61,3) (meta 2, on the stone at (0,61,4)) and a reed at (-3,61,0) (on dirt, with still water placed silently in a pit beside the dirt so it can stay, the pit capped with stone at y = 61 so the flow-cost search does not see it as a hole), both Material.circuits / plants (not solid): without the id test the flow would wash them out as items (flowIntoBlock); a ladder in the floor at (2,60,0) (meta 5, on the platform stone at x = 1): the water above neither falls into it (liquidCanDisplaceBlock) nor stops spreading (blockBlocksFlow below, BlockFlowing.java:86); a wooden door at (0,61,-3), an iron door at (3,61,-1) and a sign post at (-2,61,-2), solid materials, for the remaining ids. entity_state shows that no item is dropped.
